title: COVID-Era Changes in Lifestyle, Mental Health, and Healthcare Access Among Korean Adults
content: Objective: To quantify acute and post-acute COVID-era changes in lifestyle, mental health, healthcare access/use, and quality of life among Korean adults using national surveillance data through 2023. Methods: We analyzed publicly available aggregate data from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey for adults aged 19 years or older. Age-standardized estimates for 13 indicators were extracted for total adults, men, and women. We compared 2019 with 2020 and 2023, calculated approximate confidence intervals and false-discovery-rate-adjusted tests, and compared observed values with pre-COVID weighted trend predictions. Results: The dataset included 570 estimates. From 2019 to 2020, the largest adverse changes were unmet dental care (+9.9 percentage points), walking practice (-4.3), outpatient use (-3.5), and aerobic physical activity (-2.2). By 2023, physical-activity indicators had recovered or improved, but unmet medical care, depressive symptoms, high-risk drinking, outpatient use, and HINT-8 quality of life remained less favorable than in 2019. Unmet medical care in 2023 was 5.0 percentage points above its pre-COVID trend prediction. Conclusions: COVID-era disruption in Korea was multidimensional but uneven. Preventive policy should combine recovered behavior monitoring with continued attention to healthcare access and mental-health burden.
